instruction.text: Which phrase can be removed from the second clause?

atoms.a: I have visited the Eiffel Tower, but my brother has not visited the Eiffel Tower.

feedback.end:
Sometimes, too much repetition can actually reduce cohesion. In this example, removing the repeated phrase reduces the length of the sentence and makes it flow better. This is called ellipsis.

“I have visited the Eiffel Tower, but my brother has not.”

atoms.a: Sasha practices playing her violin after school and Sasha practices playing her violin at the weekend.

feedback.end: “Sasha practices playing her violin after school and at the weekend.”

atoms.a: Daphne would like to go to the fair, but she isn’t allowed to go to the fair.

feedback.end: “Daphne would like to go to the fair, but she isn’t allowed.”

instruction.text: Match the phrases to the sentences they have been removed from.

atoms.a: I can drive a car but my brother cannot.
Maya enjoys working in a café, but Steffan does not.
Anwar enjoys reading and playing chess.

trainers.instruction: Has ellipsis been used correctly in the sentence?

atoms.a: Danny wants to paint the bathroom blue, but Emma does not.
Tania can speak French fluently, but Jamie cannot fluently.
Samira usually takes the bus to school on Wednesdays and Thursdays.
Rosie enjoys going swimming and Rosie enjoys painting.
atoms.sound: Rosie enjoys going swimming and painting.

atoms.a: I like chocolate chip biscuits, but my sister does not like chocolate chip biscuits.
atoms.sound: I like chocolate chip biscuits, but my sister does not.

atoms.a: There is a café in the city centre and there is a café in the village.
atoms.sound: There is a café in the city centre and in the village.
